description:
## Surah An-Nazi'aat - The Draggers

(Revealed at Mecca)

46 Verses in 2 Sections

## Sections Of Surah An-Nazi'aat

1. There is a lesson in the fate of Pharaoh
2. The Doom

## An- Nazi'aat Section 1 - There Is A Lesson In The Fate Of Pharaoh

- The Resurrection sure
- There is a lesson in the fate of Pharaoh

In the name of God the Beneficent the Merciful

## An-Nazi'aat Section 2 – The Doom

- The great bounties of God to mankind,
- The Doom,
- The sufferings and the enjoyments awaiting for the wicked and righteous respectively

translations.4: ''Then those who go ahead with a foremost speed
translations.6: ''On the day on which shall quake (Commotion convulsion.) the quaking
translations.7: ''Shall follow it the quake (by the second trumpet) which shall follow
translations.10: ''They shall say (then): ''What (Parenthetical sentence referring to what people would say.) ! Shall we indeed be restored to as (we were) at first?
translations.12: ''They said: ''That then will be a return in vain (Losing - With lose.)
translations.13: ''Verily (Refer to: <{["Q", "36:29"]}>, 49, 53, <{["Q", "37:19"]}>.) , it shall be but a single (violent) blast (Or a cry - or a shaking.)
translations.14: ''When lo! they shall (all) be in the awakened state (Refer to: <{["Q", "50:22"]}>, <{["Q", "78:40"]}>, <{["Q", "75:22"]}>.)
translations.15: ''Hath not come unto thee the story (Story of Moses is recollected. Refer to: <{["Q", "20:9"]}> - <{["Q", "20:73"]}>.) of Moses?
translations.16: ''When called him his Lord in the Holy Valley (called) 'Tuva' (Refer to: <{["Q", "20:12"]}>, In a sudden change.)
translations.17: ''(Saying)-. ''Go thou (O' Moses!) unto Pharaoh (Refer to: <{["Q", "20:24"]}>.) ! verily, he hath transgressed the bounds!
translations.18: ''And say (unto him)'. ''Hast thou (Pharaoh.) (a desire) to cleanse thyself (of thy disbelief)?
translations.19: ''And I will guide thee unto thy Lord so that thou mayest fear him
translations.24: ''And said ''I am your Lord, the most High!
translations.25: ''So seized him God (Refer to: <{["Q", "20:78"]}>, <{["Q", "20:79"]}>, <{["Q", "7:135"]}> – 137.) , with the chastisement in the hereafter, and the life before (it)
translations.26: ''Verily in this there is a lesson unto him who feareth (God). (Refer to: <{["Q", "24:44"]}>.)
translations.27: ''Are ye the harder to be created, or the heaven which built He (Refer to: <{["Q", "2:29"]}>, <{["Q", "41:9"]}> - <{["Q", "41:12"]}>.) ?
translations.28: ''Raised He its heights and established (Put in an established position.) it
translations.29: ''And He darkened its night, and brought forth its noon light
translations.30: ''And the earth, afterwards he stretched forth
translations.31: ''He brought forth from it, its waters and its pasteurage
translations.32: ''And the mountains, He set them firm
translations.33: ''A provision (Refer to: <{["Q", "80:32"]}>.) for you and your cattle
translations.34: ''When cometh the Great Calamity. (The day of final Judgment.)
translations.35: The day when man shall recollect (This confirms the awakening slate mentioned in Verse <{["Q", "79:14"]}>.) (all) that he strove for
translations.36: And the hell shall be displayed unto him who seeth
translations.37: Then, as for him who hath transgressed the bounds
translations.38: And preferreth the life of this world
translations.39: Then, verily, Hell, that shall be his abode
translations.40: And as for him who feareth the standing (The justice.) of his Lord, and forbiddeth (his) self from (following) his inclinations (Submitting to God's will.)
translations.41: Then, verily, the Garden (of Paradise), that shall be his abode
translations.42: They ask thee of 'the Hour' whereto (is) anchorage (Refer to: <{["Q", "53:42"]}>, <{["Q", "7:187"]}>.) ?
translations.43: Wherein art thou of its notion (You are far away from grasping its ultimate significance. Refer to: <{["Q", "11:107"]}>, <{["Q", "11:108"]}>.) ?
translations.44: Unto thy Lord (alone) is its termination!
translations.45: Thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) art only a Warner unto him who feareth it
translations.46: It shall seem unto them, on the day when they see it, as though they tarried not in (their graves) but a (single) evening, or the following morning (Refer to: <{["Q", "10:45"]}>.)

exegesis.1:
The Arabic alphabet is used to indicate the swearing, i.e., by the angels who tear out the souls of the disbelievers from their bodies. The beginning of this Surah is like that of Surah 77.

The swearing by the angels and the other forces and the elements in nature, might not give the true sense of the gravity of the act to those ignorant of the greatness of the things or the phenomenon but those who know how great and mysterious are the things and the functioning of the natural phenomena would realise the seriousness or the importance of the occasion for God to do it - and how great and vital the thing must be to mankind that the Gracious God announces of it with so much stress. Though the souls of the disbelievers are loath to part with their physical body, they are dragged out violently by force.

In the first, second and the third verses the reference is to the forces which are working preparatory to put an object into motion, i.e., to draw forth to remove obstacles, to put into motion. Then in verse 4, competition starts. Hence the need of administration referred to in verse 5. The question is whether the forces are angelic, natural or human. Considering the fact that the chain of the forces working in the universe reverts to God and one proceeds the other harmoniously, there is no reason for restricting to any particular force<{["F", 1]}>. The same is throughout these verses. (A.P.)
exegesis.2: By the angels who gently cause the soul of the righteous ones to get released of their confinement of their bodies. In contrast to the disbelievers and the wicked ones, the souls of the believers and the righteous ones, only await their release from the material bodies and its commitments. Hence the souls themselves pass out of their bodies willingly and the angel makes the task easy and pleasant.
exegesis.3: By the angels who are busy moving about briskly in executing their duties in the management or the administration of the universe.
exegesis.4: By the angels which race with each other in executing the will of the Lord to His satisfaction and pleasure.
exegesis.5: By the angels who manage the affairs of the universe in a systematic way.
exegesis.6: The reference is to the violent commotion, the greatly agitated state of convulsion that will be affected at the dawn of the Day of Judgment which everything in the universe shall experience.
exegesis.7: The change that the whole of this present world will undergo. A new state of life will be established in the place of the present one.
exegesis.10:
This refers to the deniers denying such a sure event which shall take place.

A parenthetical sentence referring to what people sat now in this life - doubting about resurrection. (A. P.)
exegesis.14: Said the Holy Prophet: - ''_Annas Niyammon Fai'za Maatoo intabaho_", i.e., People are asleep, they will awake when they die. To which reference is made in <{["Q", "50:22"]}>. (A.P.)
exegesis.27: Man is reminded of his insignificant physical position in the universe. When the heavens with all their heavenly bodies will succumb to the will of the Lord and vanish at His will - of what consideration could be man who is nothing more than an insignificant germ in the set-up of the universe.
exegesis.28: The mystery of the existence of the heavens and the wonderful heavenly bodies in them, with the perfection in their form and the perfect harmony, with which each one works with the other, was brought into existence by God, and is worked at His will.
exegesis.30: 'Dab.' here means further expansion<{["F", 1]}> of its surface long after the creation of the earth and the heavenly bodies. It may refer to the last layer of the earth which produces food for men and the animals. (A.P.)
exegesis.31: The ready supply of water through the underground springs and wells and the wonderful arrangement of rain from heaven and the evaporation of the water from seas; all these are the unquestionable proofs of the Wisdom and Might of the Creator.
exegesis.35:
Every act and motive of evert one, will be laid bare to each individual to account for.

This confirms the awakening state referred to in in Verse <{["Q", "79:14"]}> (A.P.).
exegesis.37: Those who wilfully persisted in transgressing the prescribed limits, will have the abiding chastisement and those who were the victims of the common weakness in the human being and who yielded to the human frailty, will have to face the balancing of their evil with their goodness<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.40: Note the key to heaven and the blissful life therein, has been shown and that is the control of the self and refraining from low desires, abstaining from the forbidden.
exegesis.43:
The time limit in terms of the state of existence after life or on the Day of Judgment, is quite different from that of our calculation in the present life. God alone knows the extent or its duration. The whole matter lies in the will of the Lord<{["F", 1]}>.

You are far away from grasping its ultimate significance. (A.P.)
exegesis.44:
The duty of an apostle of God ends with warning those who want to avail of the message and the admonition. No apostle of God is responsible for the conduct and character of the people.

It indicates that the whole system of universe is in motion and in the state of ever becoming. It is He to Whom the motion terminates. There is nothing in the whole system of the Universe to be termed eternal. Hence '_Hudoose Zamani al-Aalam'_, i.e., The universe being as a whole and past being created from naught. (A.P.)
exegesis.45: None knows the extent of the passage of time<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.46:
Refers to the last state of the awakening when the conscious self gets out of the bounds, time and space, the whole system of the four-dimensional state will appear to him and even less than a part of an ordinary day - to which Eqbal says: Referring to the stars addressing man - saying ''_Thy century unto Us is only a moment and thine Ocean unto Us is only a drop. We are seeing and passing"._

Qur'an says the day shall come - man will be in a position to say the same to the whole heavenly bodies. (A.P.)
